web.title_en: CVE-2026-6307: Missing Signature Comparison Causes Wasm Return Type Mismatch
web.description_en: When TurboFan inlines two JS-to-Wasm call sites with different return types into the same function, the frame state equality check omits a comparison of Wasm signatures, causing two distinct frame states to be treated as identical. After an optimization rollback, the return value is materialized with the wrong type—object addresses are read as integers, and integers are misinterpreted as object pointers.

web.title: Ruby Fixes Three Regex Engine Bugs Responsible for Four Critical GitLab RCE Flaws
web.description: Ruby has released versions 4.0.9, 3.4.12, and 3.3.13 to fix three bugs in Onigmo, the regular expression engine built into the language. The bugs lie behind four critical security flaws that GitLab patched over the past month.   GitLab found that a specially crafted pattern could corrupt memory while Ruby compiles it, potentially leading to code execution on its own servers.   Ruby says any application that builds a regular expression from text an attacker controls is affected, not just GitLab.   Which Applications Are Affected   In  its advisory , Ruby said an application is affected only if it compiles a regular expression from a string an attacker controls. That happens when a program passes such a string to Regexp.new, Regexp.union or Regexp.compile, or places it inside a pattern through interpolation, as in /#{input}/. web.description: PHP has warned of another way an attacker could run code on a web server, two days after it shipped emergency fixes for the critical PHP2Shell flaws.   The new issue, assigned CVE-2026-115560 , affects only web applications configured in an unusual way, and PHP considers it an unlikely risk. The project is not issuing an emergency fix for it. Instead, it recommends turning off a feature called session upload progress  until a fix is available in the next routine release. web.title: Critical Flaw in Python’s Popular Pillow Image Library Allows Code Execution via a Crafted Image
web.description: Pillow , the most widely used image library for Python, can be made to run operating system commands on a server by specifying the name of a file it is told to open.   The flaw,  CVE-2026-112900 , is in the way Pillow handles EPS images, which it opens by passing the file's name to Ghostscript , a separate program it runs to turn the image into pixels, without checking the name first.   Ghostscript can read a name chosen by an attacker as instructions rather than as a file, and point it to a second file that carries commands to run. Pillow's maintainers fixed it in  version 13.0.0 , released on October 16.   Pillow turns up almost everywhere Python handles images: web upload forms, avatar and thumbnail tools, document and PDF pipelines, and most machine-learning projects pull it in. web.description: AI agents paying for API calls with the  x402 SDKs  could sign a payment for their full balance of a supported token if a malicious API asked for it,  security firm V12 said  on October 22.   The cause was the SDKs' default client, which set no spending limit until releases on August 18 added one.
